events.text: Tingmissartoq was the name given to a Lockheed Model 8 Sirius flown by Charles and Anne Morrow Lindbergh.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Tingmissartoq was the name given to a Lockheed Model 8 Sirius flown by Charles and Anne Morrow Lindbergh in the 1930s

events.text: The plane was christened by an Inuit boy in Godthaab (Nuuk), Greenland, who painted the word on its side.
events.subject: self
events.quote: the plane was thus christened by an Inuit boy in Godthaab ( Nuuk ) , Greenland

events.text: The Lindberghs planned to fly to the Orient via the Great Circle Route.
events.subject: self
events.quote: 1931 , when the Lindberghs planned to fly to the Orient via the Great Circle Route

events.text: The trip began in North Haven, Maine.
events.subject: self
events.quote: It began in North Haven , Maine

events.text: The final stop on Lotus Lake near Nanking was made on September 19.
events.subject: self
events.quote: its final stop on Lotus Lake near Nanking made on September 19

events.text: Tingmissartoq was to see action again.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Tingmissartoq was to see action again in 1933

events.text: Lindbergh took off from New York City in the rebuilt craft.
events.subject: self
events.quote: he took off from New York City on July 9 in the rebuilt craft

events.text: The Lindberghs returned to New York.
events.subject: self
events.quote: They returned to New York on December 19

events.text: Tingmissartoq was on display in the American Museum of Natural History in New York City until 1955.
events.subject: self
events.quote: on display in the American Museum of Natural History in New York City until 1955

events.text: Tingmissartoq was acquired by the National Museum of the United States Air Force in Dayton, Ohio.
